description: issue #775 (review gate, QA finding N7): `every true [ … ]` -- a tick count that is neither a number nor a word, the twin of `wait/wait-non-number-list-type-error` (which covers `list`). Between them the pair pins the two remaining COMPARABLE arms of `params.actual` for the shared whole-number check: before them the corpus pinned only `number` and `word` across the whole stack (`wait`, `every`, `repeat`, `random`), so an implementation could report anything for a boolean or a list and still pass the full stack-neutral corpus -- confirmed by mutation. The `dict` and `record` arms are deliberately NOT fixtured -- their `params.value` currently serialises to JSON lossily, so a fixture would make that lossy shape normatively binding; they are pinned by unit test instead, and the reasoning is recorded in this directory's README. `spec/execution-model.md`'s value model makes `boolean` a first-class Core value, and no coercion rule can rescue it (unlike a word), so this is `ol-type` outright with no wholeness question to reach. The check fails BEFORE registration, so no `primitive` event is emitted and no handler is registered; only the registration instruction precedes the diagnostic, and the span covers just the count argument.

diagnostics.message: every needs a whole number, but got a boolean.
